messages:
OpsBot: INCIDENT ALERT: inference-throttle-surge detected in us-west-2. 3xx/4xx spike + token rate > 2x baseline. Pager routed to @oncall. Incident ID: INC-2026-0421
Alex C.: seeing it. queue_depth jump on inference-pool-3, a few customers reporting elevated latencies. taking it.
Samir: on it. Any automated fallback kicked in?
Alex C.: fallback routed to smaller model variants but many requests still hitting throttles (429). Looks like throttles are coming from autoscale lag + KV-cache hot keys.
Maria L.: support reports 5 customers with errors (one enterprise customer on dedicated). sending list to ops.
Kate (support): pasted customer list in DM. Two customers on dedicated, three on hosted. They see failures in request logs: "throttle: quota_exceeded".
Nate P.: quick mitigation proposal: 1) increase pool size for inference-pool-3 by +3 nodes 2) enable temporary route to warm read-only pool 3) patch alert thresholds to reduce noise while we stabilize. Thoughts?
Lia: +1 to scale up now. I'll push scale.
Alex C.: Lia — run rwdctl scale pool inference-pool-3 --add 3 please. Monitor queue_depth while scaling.
Lia: running: ```bash
rwdctl scale pool inference-pool-3 --target=12
# started at 2273456822
```
Lia: new nodes reporting ready. latency trending down slightly. queue_depth still peaky though.
Samir: rolling back aggressive batching for _high_qps_ route, set max_batch_tokens=1024 -> 512 to reduce burst amplification. Pushing config now.
Alex C.: applied. Observed immediate drop in per-request tokens/sec and fewer KV cache thrash logs. Throttles dropped from ~12% to ~4% in 2m.
Maria L.: customer impact update: Enterprise A on dedicated still seeing intermittent 429s; support routed traffic to their dedicated fallback and engagement team notified.
Kate (support): I've opened a support incident for Enterprise A and linked legal/sales.
Samir: alert tuning notes while we're stabilizing: current queue_depth alert fires at 800 for 30s -> too noisy during transient bursts. Propose: change to 1200 for 120s and add a secondary alert for sustained tokens/sec > 1.5x baseline for 180s. Also add a dashboard tile for per-customer throttle rate.
Alex C.: sounds reasonable. We should also add an automatic suppression rule for expected throttles during autoscale operations for 5m to reduce pager noise.
Lia: created dashboard: "inference-pool-3 — queue / throttle per customer" and pinned to oncall overview.
Samir: patch for alert rule (to be applied after incident): ```yaml
alert: HighInferenceQueueDepth
expr: sum(queue_depth{pool="inference-pool-3"}) > 1200
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  runbook: /runbooks/autoscale-throttle-mitigation
```
Samir: and secondary: ```yaml
alert: SustainedTokenRateSpike
expr: rate(tokens_processed[2m]) > 1.5 * avg_rate_over_1h
for: 3m
labels:
  severity: ticket
```
Nate P.: creating a follow-up ticket to validate the KV cache hotkey detection (likely need prefix caching and per-client circuit breaker). Assigning to eng-runtime.
Alex C.: post-incident action items: 1) alert retune as Samir suggested 2) add per-customer throttle dashboard 3) run a chaos load test to validate autoscale latency 4) explore adaptive batching knob for high QPS clients. Owning: Samir, Lia, Eng-runtime, SRE.
Maria L.: ETA on postmortem doc? We should include customer impact timeline and mitigation steps for support/litigation.
Nate P.: I'll draft postmortem today and include timeline + graphs. Sharing link in this thread when ready.
Kate (support): Customers notified with status updates. No escalations to execs so far.
OpsBot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Throttle rate reduced to baseline. Incident state: mitigating -> monitoring. End time: 2273456859.
Alex C.: leaving notes in incident channel. If anything regresses, poke oncall. Great job everyone :thumbsup:
Samir: quick runbook change suggested: add explicit check for tokens/sec surge to delay batch growth. I'll PR to runbooks repo.
Lia: will keep the dashboard pinned for next 24h.
Nate P.: postmortem link: https://rwd.internal/postmortems/INC-2026-0421 (draft).
Alex C.: closing thread after postmortem goes live.
